items.definition: To judge how well a student has learnt something, or to judge the quality or level of something.
examples: Teachers assess pupils through projects as well as exams.
The panel will assess every application before the interviews.

items.definition: A piece of work that a student is given to do as part of a course.
examples: The history assignment has to be handed in by Monday morning.

items.definition: In Britain, a place where students aged sixteen or over study for exams or practical qualifications, or one of the parts of some universities.
examples: After school she went to college to train as an electrician.

trap.en: A college is not a primary or secondary school. Children aged five to sixteen go to school.
trap.es: «Colegio» es school. College es para mayores de dieciséis años: formación profesional o bachillerato, o parte de una universidad.

items.definition: Required by a rule or law, so that you have no choice.
examples: Maths is compulsory until the age of sixteen in most schools.

items.definition: Work that students do during a course, which counts towards their final mark instead of, or as well as, an exam.
examples: Forty per cent of the mark comes from coursework, and the rest from the final exam.

items.definition: The subjects and topics that a school or course teaches.
examples: Many parents want financial skills to be added to the school curriculum.

trap.en: A curriculum is what is taught in a school. The document you send to an employer is a CV.
trap.es: El «currículum» que mandas a una empresa es a CV. Curriculum es el plan de estudios de un centro.

items.definition: A long piece of written work on a subject you have researched, usually done at the end of a degree.
examples: She is writing her dissertation on urban transport in the nineteenth century.

items.definition: To leave school, college or a course before you have finished it.
examples: He dropped out of university after the first year because of the cost.
The number of students who drop out has fallen.

items.definition: To officially join a course, school or university, or to put someone's name on its list of students.
examples: I've enrolled on an evening course in Italian.
Parents must enrol their children before the end of May.

items.definition: To finish a university degree successfully.
examples: She graduated in 2019 with a degree in biology.

items.definition: A talk given to a large group of students or the public to teach them about a subject.
examples: The lecture on climate policy lasted an hour and a half.

trap.en: A lecture is a talk given by a speaker. The act of reading, or something you read, is reading.
trap.es: «Lectura» es reading. Lecture es una conferencia o una clase magistral en la universidad.

items.definition: The act of using another person's words or ideas as if they were your own, without saying where they came from.
examples: The university takes plagiarism very seriously and uses software to detect it.

items.definition: To study again what you have already learnt, to prepare for an exam.
examples: I can't go out tonight; I need to revise for my chemistry test.

items.definition: Money given to a student by an organisation to help pay for their studies.
examples: He won a scholarship to study engineering abroad.

items.definition: Teaching, or the money you pay for being taught, especially at a university.
examples: Tuition fees have risen sharply over the past decade.
She gets private tuition in maths twice a week.
